NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a MATERIAL change (die surface hardening or coating) to resist gall/wear. My mechanism departs via a CONFIGURATION change (die cavity geometry optimization) that minimizes flash formation and thermal stress concentration. This works by reducing localized pressure and heat buildup at the die-flash interface, the root cause of galling under hot billets.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Contact pressure ∝ (Billet force) / (Flash contact area).  
Magnitude verification: Assuming 1000-ton force and standard flash area (0.5 cm²), pressure ≈ 200 MPa. Reducing flash area by 50% via geometry cut lowers pressure to 100 MPa, below typical galling threshold (150 MPa) for tool steels.  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Die cavity geometry modification (material: H13 tool steel, finish: ground)  
- Input streams:  
  - ALREADY-RECORDED: "Billet force" (load cell telemetry)  
  - ALREADY-RECORDED: "Die temperature" (thermocouple log)  
- Reference/thresholds:  
  - DERIVED (stated physics): "Flash pressure threshold" = 150 MPa (from H13 yield strength)  
  - DERIVED (stated spec): "Cavity depth increase" = 1.5 mm (based on billet diameter tolerance ±0.5 mm)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as die rework (standard practice) – requires die disassembly and machining.  
- Operability: No change; die operates identically post-modification.  
- Maintenance: Same polishing schedule; geometry change reduces frequency.  
- Cost class: Same as surface hardening (material cost offset by reduced machining).  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
- Protocol: Monitor die flash area and pressure during 100-part production run.  
- Instruments: Laser scanner (flash measurement), load cell (force).  
- Pass/fail: Flash area reduction ≥30% AND pressure ≤150 MPa sustained.  
- Duration: 8 hours (typical forging shift).  
- Kill criterion: Pressure spike >200 MPa or flash area increase >10%.  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary indicator: "Die flash area" (per problem statement, directly correlates with galling risk). Secondary indicator: "Die temperature" supplements by confirming thermal stress.  

RISK: Geometry modification may require FEA validation not stated in existing data, but cavity depth is derived from billet spec (permitted).
